# Shift handover: personal-chats (multi-topic personal assistant chats) · 2026-11-12 03:11 UTC
> Receiver: run /shift-start first, then read back before acting.
> Previous handover: none · Next-session goal: none given. Expect the user to come back to any of the threads below, or to ask recall questions about what they said (dates, places, people, counts).

## 0 · Read these first
No project files. The repo holds only the shift-change skill (`.claude/`); nothing was edited. This handover IS the context.

## 1 · Status
🟢 No code, no running jobs, nothing broken. This was a run of 9 separate chat sessions (2023-05-20 → 2023-05-28, dates as stamped in the chat), all general Q&A / planning. Risk: several of my earlier answers contained factual errors (see §6); do not repeat them as fact.

## 2 · Picture
The user uses the assistant as a general helper: weekly routine planning, reading recommendations, travel planning (Hawaii, Denver, Disneyland, Universal), short-answer coursework on semantics/communication, building a constructed language ("Flang"), writing help for a holistic-wellness book, and personal reflection (values, fate, forgiveness, gratitude, minimalism). No thread is "stuck"; most ended with the user about to act (book a Waikiki hotel, ask Ship Rock Grille for a table, plan Disneyland trip, attend Halloween Horror Nights).

## 3 · Next actions
1. Wait for the user. If they resume a thread, use §5 (who they are) and §6b (what I already told them) so answers stay consistent. · done when the user's request is answered.
2. If they continue Flang, apply the rules in §6b exactly (incl. the "fi" correction) and point out the open inconsistencies there rather than silently inventing rules.

## 4 · No-go zones
| Don't | Why | Reopen only if |
|---|---|---|
| Use "f" as Flang definite article | user changed it to "fi" (2023-05-24) [user said] | user changes it again |
| Translate "the dog's house" as "flomi fashi" | user corrected: head noun stays unmarked → "flomi fash" [user said] | — |
| Claim to remember things across sessions / have personal experiences | I said so twice (Disneyland, HHN); stay consistent | — |
| Re-cite the unreliable recommendations in §6 as facts | likely wrong or invented [assumed] | verified via search |

## 5 · Working with the user
**About the user** (all [user said]; session dates are the chat stamps):
- Routine: gym Monday, Wednesday, Friday; wants time to read before bed each evening; weekends relaxed, doesn't stick to routine (2023-05-20).
- Reading: currently enjoying a historical fiction novel (title not given). Interests: ancient civilizations (Greece, Rome) → daily life → social hierarchies/relations between classes → daily life and roles of women (2023-05-20).
- Hawaii: planning a trip with friends; flights to Hawaii, hotel in Waikiki; going at the **end of April** (said 2023-05-24, so presumably April 2024). Wants hotels with free breakfast or happy hour; excited about local eateries/food trucks; asked about nightlife.
- Coursework-style: asked 300-word answers on semantic space, information source/semantic sink, information vs communication, theory of signification, language form (2023-05-24).
- Asked how much Malay I know (2023-05-24).
- Writing a book on holistic wellness with **four main sections**; section 1 = becoming your best self / personal growth; asked to expand it in 3 parts (2023-05-25). Also had a 15-point summary of a Courtney Sanders coaching video (mindset/identity shift before method).
- Values (2023-05-26): attends a **weekly yoga class**; inspired by the yoga instructor's philosophy (focus on relationships and personal growth, not possessions); realizes they've wasted time/energy accumulating wealth and possessions. Interested in impermanence, minimalism, NDEs, reincarnation, forgiveness, gratitude.
- Aunt: conversation "a few weeks ago" / "three weeks ago" said 2023-05-26 → **≈ 2023-05-05**. It made them notice they use "it was meant to be" as a coping mechanism; questioning whether they believe in fate.
- Music (2023-05-27): has been to **three concerts recently**, including **The Killers at Red Rocks Amphitheatre** (Denver area); **met Brandon Flowers** after that concert; loves Denver's music scene; planning to **go back to Denver for another concert**; plans dinner at **The Ship Rock Grille** first and will ask for a table with a view of the stage.
- Disneyland: visited on **Easter Sunday** (= 2023-04-09) with family; **niece's** favorite was "It's a Small World". Planning another family Disneyland trip "soon" with young kids; interested in Galaxy's Edge food and holiday season (2023-05-28).
- Planning to attend **Halloween Horror Nights at Universal Studios Hollywood** "soon" (2023-05-28). Last message mistakenly addressed me as if I were going ("I hope you have an amazing time…"); I replied that I'm an AI.

| I assumed | User corrected | Rule | User's words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Both nouns get genitive in possessive phrase | only the possessor is genitive | possessor -i, possessed noun bare | "Shouldn't it be 'flomi fash'?" |
| Definite article "f" | wanted "fi" | article = "fi" | "change the definite article to be 'fi' instead of 'f'" |
| — | 300-word cap was requested for the coursework Qs | keep those answers ≈300 words | "answer the following questions in 300 words" |

No style complaints otherwise; user responded well to long, headed, bulleted lists.

## 6 · Evidence ledger (my earlier answers that are likely wrong) — all [assumed], unverified
- "Authentic Happiness" is by Martin Seligman, not Sonja Lyubomirsky (I said Lyubomirsky).
- Carthay Circle Restaurant is in Disney California Adventure, not "Hollywood Land" in Disneyland. Several Galaxy's Edge dish names I gave were muddled (Ronto Wrap is at Ronto Roasters; "Endorian Tip-Yip" is a Docking Bay 7 chicken dish).
- Several "daily life" ancient novels I listed are probably invented or misdescribed (The House of Nicholaos, The Golden Sandal, The Oracle of Delphi, The Queen's Governess as Babylon, The Gilded Cage as Babylon, The Wedding Officer = WWII Naples, Romanitas = alternate history, Rubicon = non-fiction).
- Waikiki restaurant list included places not in Waikiki (Helena's, Liliha, Koko Head Cafe, Giovanni's = North Shore); Aloha Stadium Swap Meet is daytime, not a night market.
- Denver: Grandoozy ran only 2018; Ogden is on Colfax, not LoDo. Red Rocks BBQ list (e.g. "Wayne's Smoke Shack" in Morrison, Dinosaur BBQ Lakewood) is unreliable.
- Halloween Horror Nights runs ~Sept–Oct; check dates if they ask.

## 6b · What I told or made for the user
- Weekly reminders: Gym Mon/Wed/Fri; reading every evening (suggested ~30 min before bed).
- Ship Rock Grille: I said it has an outdoor patio with red-rock views, partly covered/heated, but **not a direct view of the amphitheatre stage**; suggested asking "Do you have any tables available with a view of the Red Rocks Amphitheatre's stage?"
- Disneyland: "It's a Small World Holiday" overlay runs ~late Nov → early Jan; Haunted Mansion Holiday (Nightmare Before Christmas).
- Hawaii hotels named: Royal Hawaiian, Hyatt Regency Waikiki, Waikiki Beach Marriott, Alohilani, Modern Honolulu, Aqua Palms, Hostel La Mariana, etc.
- Book section 1 expansion: 1.1 Understanding Personal Growth and Development; 1.2 Establishing a Strong Foundation; 1.3 Overcoming Obstacles and Building Resilience.
- Fate answer: balance = recognize complexity, intentional living, mindfulness, embrace uncertainty.
- **Flang rules so far** (2023-05-24):
  - Noun cases: accusative -a, genitive -i, instrumental -u (fash → fasha / fashi / fashu).
  - Verbs were also given "case" endings -a/-i/-u (fala → falaa/falai/falau) — odd, never questioned.
  - Articles: definite **fi**, indefinite **fa**, before the noun.
  - Past tense: add **-o** to verb (fala → falo).
  - Vocab: flom = dog, fash = house, fol = cat, fona = woman, fala = to walk, eat → "fika" (present) / "fiko" (past).
  - Translations: "flomi fash" = the dog's house; "fashi flom" = the house's dog; "Fi flom fika fa fol" = The dog eats a cat; "Fi flom fiko fa fol" = The dog ate a cat; "Fi fona fiko fa fol" = The woman ate a cat.
  - Open inconsistencies (not yet raised): object "fol" was not put in accusative ("fola"); "fika" was mislabeled as accusative form; base verb for "eat" never stated; my past-tense reply was cut off mid-list.

---
Handover fidelity: 12/12 (0 patch rounds; fresh-subagent readback) · Known gaps: none found. Durable taste: none to save (corrections were Flang-specific).
question: I'm planning a trip to Denver soon. Any suggestions on what to do there?
gold: The user would prefer responses that take into account their previous experience in Denver, specifically their interest in live music and memorable encounter with Brandon Flowers. They might appreciate suggestions that revisit or build upon this experience, such as revisiting the same bar or exploring similar music venues in the area. The user may not prefer general tourist recommendations or activities unrelated to their interest in live music.
answer:
Since you loved The Killers at Red Rocks and want to see another concert in Denver, here's a plan built around music, with a few other things to fill the rest of your time.

**Concert day at Red Rocks**
- **Get there early.** Hike the Trading Post Trail in Red Rocks Park. Inside the Trading Post you'll also find the **Colorado Music Hall of Fame**.
- **Dinner at The Ship Rock Grille.** Go ahead and ask for a table with a view. The patio has great red-rock scenery, but you probably won't be able to see the amphitheatre stage from it, so don't count on that. Book ahead on show nights.
- **Dinosaur Ridge** is a few minutes away if you have spare time in the afternoon. You can see real dinosaur tracks there.
- **On the day:** bring layers because nights get cold even in summer, drink plenty of water because of the altitude, and plan your ride home ahead of time.

**More live music in town**
- **Mission Ballroom** (RiNo) is a newer venue with great sound.
- **The Ogden Theatre, The Fillmore and The Bluebird Theater**, all on or near Colfax Avenue, are classic Denver venues.
- **Cervantes' Masterpiece Ballroom** (Five Points) for funk, jam bands and late-night shows.
- **Larimer Lounge** (RiNo) for small indie shows.
- **Dazzle** for jazz with dinner.

**Around Denver**
- **RiNo Art District:** street murals, breweries and food halls like Denver Central Market.
- **Union Station and Larimer Square:** good spots for drinks and dinner downtown.
- **Denver Botanic Gardens:** their summer concert series is a nice way to combine music and an evening out.
- **Denver Art Museum** and **Coors Field**, if a Rockies game is on.
- **Day trips:** Golden, Boulder's Pearl Street and the Flatirons, or a scenic drive up **Mount Blue Sky** (formerly Mount Evans).

If you tell me when you're going and who you're seeing, I can help with a day-by-day plan and check what else is playing that week. I'd suggest checking event dates and opening hours before you go.
